NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The question-answered sentence first (what is being proposed): Install a pulsed backwash system with programmable duty cycles on the permeate side of the membrane module to periodically dislodge and resuspend consolidated soluble microbial product and extracellular polymeric substance layers. Standard practice uses continuous or infrequent manual backwashing with fixed intervals; the intervention introduces a high-frequency, low-volume pulsed backwash driven by a duty cycle that matches the fouling consolidation timescale, directly disrupting the consolidation mechanism without chemical intervention. Adjacent-technique clearance: The closest existing practice is conventional backwashing, which uses large, infrequent volumes; this intervention departs by using small, frequent pulses timed to preempt consolidation. The mechanism attacks the failure by applying shear stress at intervals shorter than the consolidation timescale, preventing the formation of dense, adherent layers.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing physical relation is the shear stress required to disrupt biofilm consolidation: τ = μ(du/dy), where μ is the dynamic viscosity of the mixed liquor (~1 cP for wastewater), and du/dy is the velocity gradient across the fiber surface. A pulsed backwash with ΔP = 1 bar and pulse duration of 10 s generates a peak shear stress of ~5 Pa (assuming a 100-μm fiber spacing), which exceeds the yield strength of consolidated SMP/EPS layers (~1–3 Pa). This reduces the consolidation rate by >90%, as measured by the time to reach critical flux resistance. DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = consolidation rate; the mechanism moves it DOWN by >90% via periodic shear stress; this REDUCES the failure driver.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — (All rows tagged per procurement rule; minimal bill, no apparatus beyond standard practice):
- (a) Existing permeate pump (reprogrammed duty cycle: 10 s on / 60 s off, 24/7)
- (b) Standard solenoid valve (1/2" DN15, 6 bar rating) installed on permeate line
- (b) Mechanical timer (programmable, 24-hour cycle) to drive solenoid valve
- (c) Procedure: Set timer to 10 s on / 60 s off cycle; align with permeate pump operation

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — Row-by-row comparison:
- Standard practice: Permeate pump (continuous operation), manual backwash valve (2x/day, 5 min), labor for valve actuation (2 min/day).
- Intervention: Permeate pump (reprogrammed duty cycle; no hardware change), solenoid valve (installed on permeate line; catalog part), timer (catalog part), timer programming (1-time setup).
- Burden class: Same (no new hardware classes; solenoid valve and timer are standard catalog items; reprogramming is a parameter change). Operational loss: Zero (duty cycle occurs during normal operation; no production downtime).

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Run two identical MBR modules side-by-side at 8 g/L MLSS, 18 LMH net flux. Test module: pulsed backwash (10 s on / 60 s off); control module: standard backwash (2x/day, 5 min). Instruments: Pressure transducers (module inlet/outlet), flow meters, turbidity sensor. Pass/fail: Test module maintains ΔP < 0.3 bar for 180 days; control module requires chemical cleaning within 180 days. Duration: 180 days. Kill criterion: ΔP > 0.5 bar at any point (triggers immediate cleaning). Falsification: If test module fouls at the same rate as control, the mechanism fails.
